title: The Five Emanations and the Body of the Proprium
description: T25 names the Lord's five emanations going forth one beside another: from the Lord's mind comes the recognized-and-returned love; from his thought, the life-bearing principle; from his teaching, the beloved instruction; from his counsel, pure receivability; from his reflection, the gathering principle. T26 likens the same Lord at three registers: the Divine Human as a man whose property was scattered who comes after his own; the operative power as a great furnace and warrior who lifts the king's son out of captivity; the call as a great man who comes after his wealth and brings what was held back into the very country where she had been kept. T27 anatomizes the body the proprium takes when fully formed: head as ravenous love, wings as upward thoughts, feet as lower cravings, belly as digesting darkness, loins as sense-knowledges — five forms of one self-claiming, hard against natural truth, oscillating between fire and cold.
